text_fidelity_a: N NEVO RHINO Hydration Backpack, Hydration Pack, Insulated Hiking Backpack with Water Bladder 3L for Hiking Cycling Running Biking Camping I purchased this hydration backpack with the 3L water bladder in mid April, in preparation for a long US roadtrip with several visits to national and state parks. With lots of hiking in hot weather, I needed a reliable hydration source. Unfortunately this product wasn’t it. I tested the bladder system at home, and it seemed OK. However, the bladder didn’t survive its first real world test. In Canyonlands, Utah, with 100+ degree weather, two things happened: (1) the suction end got punctured within minutes. It still worked and didn’t leak, so I kept on using it throughout the day. (2) At the end of the day, back at the hotel, when I tried to refill the bladder I couldn’t get the bladder seal off. The hard plastic handle/seal doesn’t budge at all, and it almost seems as if it has fused closed (I don’t think that’s possible, but the reality is I can’t slide it at all, and yes, I am doing it in the right direction.) Bottom line: I am at the beginning of a series of hikes, left without this key component of my hydration system (fortunately I have backups, though I’ll miss having a hydration backpack/water bladder, and it’s beyond the return window, so I’m out of money as well. I know that the vast majority of the reviews are positive (that’s why I bought this item!), but based on my experience I cannot recommend this product. One star from me.

text_fidelity_a:
Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch I had high hopes for this device. I think it's aimed at people who don't want a gadget to play with, but a useful and attractive minimalist activity tracker. It qualifies as attractive and, if all you want to do is count steps, it is useful. Ultimately, I had to quit wearing it because it caused a severe rash on my wrist under one side of the band. I have reached out to Withings and I will update this review when my issue is resolved (or not). At this point I just want to return it for the following reasons:

1. The rash was severe. I've now gone 2 weeks without wearing the watch and it has barely diminished. I'm not allergic to silicone, so I wonder what chemicals are in or on the band.
2. The lack of contrast between the hands and the face result in a watch I can only read in good light. In a dimly lit room it is completely unreadable.
3. A big reason the watch appealed to me is that I can wear it while swimming. It is supposed to log swim time, but it was unreliable to the point of being useless for this purpose.
4. I was intrigued by the sleep tracking, but it has quirks that make me doubt it's usefulness. For example, if I sit on the couch reading or watching TV for an hour before bed, sometimes it logs this as sleep, including deep sleep.

The watch counts from 50% to 20% less steps than my Samsung app. I can't say which is more accurate. I like the idea of an elegant and simple tracker/watch, and this was almost it. Ultimately nothing else matters because I can't wear it. The negatives add up to the point that I'm not interested in resolving the rash problem with a different band.

Update: I reached out to Withings. They responded quickly and seemed genuinely concerned. They dealt with my problem promptly and fairly. I'm upping my review from 2 stars to 3 stars because of the customer service.
text_fidelity_b: Withings ActivitÃ Steel - Activity and Sleep Tracking Watch

I think this is the price point (in Daiwa) where you get the best value. I think when getting a 200 dollar reel you are at the point of diminishing returns. I use this for 6 pound test and a Daiwa RG300AB for heavier test. I forget which is the "better" series, but to me the quality between the two is indistinguishable and I believe you will be happy with any reel from either series.

There is no noise when reeling, no line twist, no wobble, and they both feel like a million bucks. I've been debating about taking the entire thing apart and lubing it myself, which many fisherman do as maintenance, however I don't know if there is any benefit. I take apart and service wristwatches with well over 100 parts, but am worried I may not reassemble this correctly. Maybe I shouldn't be worried.
text_fidelity_b: Daiwa Revros Spinning Fishing Reels

text_fidelity_a:
M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube You see all of these reviews and they all start to sound the same, so I'll tell you where I'm coming from, my thoughts on the rod, and give my verdict.
I love fishing. There's nothing I'd rather do on the whole world. Nothing. You know what I mean... Lol! I've been fishing for decades, but have only been fly fishing for 3 years or so. I have several spinning rods in the $100-$200 range, and they are amazing. Unfortunately a $200 fly rod isn't the same as a $200 spinning rod. You can easily spend $3000 on a high end fly rod!

Well, I don't want to. I don't think it's necessary. But I've been fishing long enough that I can feel a great rod when I handle one. That's good, because I've seen lots of very expensive rods that were trash, and a few hidden gems that punched WAY above their weight. The Maxcatch Premiere line is one of those hidden gems. I picked this 3WT up just to check out, and after I effortlessly my fly 55' and landed it precisely where I wanted it. Over and over again. I mean it is so accurate that it's almost boring lol! And it's a $55 rod!

The blank is very sensitive, very light, very well finished and attractive, and the cork and dark chromed accents are beautiful. I'm surprised at how nice the cork is at this price point!

So I fish. A lot. I used to sell fishing equipment for a living, and I've handle a lot of gear. Is this Maxcatch a Loop or high end Sage? No. But it's also not $400-$900. However, I'd put this up against ANY Reddington, Fenwick, or lower end Sage any day and put money on the Maxcatch.

Get this rod. You'll be glad you did. You'll catch a ton of fish if you do your part, because this is a magnificent tool at an amazing price!

EDIT: I caught that monster 'Bow on the 4wt. Great fight! The rod was bent in half for 5 minutes, and held up great. And I felt every run, head shake, and dive. Great rods!
text_fidelity_b: M MAXIMUMCATCH Maxcatch 3-12wt Medium-Fast Action Premier Fly Fishing Rod-IM8 Carbon Blank for High Performance,with AA Cork Grip Hard Chromed Guides and Cordura Tube

text_fidelity_a:
TIMBUK2 Command Laptop Backpack, Black [[VIDEOID:mo363W3UY9IZ8Y3]]Let me start by saying that I've been using various Timbuk2's bags since the mid 1990s. While the prices may be a bit high, I've consistently found their bags to be well built, durable, with excellent water protection. In fact, I recently used one of their camera backpacks on a three week trip across Japan where the bag was subjected to a number of downpours; no water ever pierced the bag's envelope.

In terms of size, the volume of this bag is comparable to the laptop briefcases that came with laptops in the 1990s through the early aughts. As you'll see in my video, the laptop is housed in a compartment on the back of the bag in a heavily padded sleeve. In the video I have a 13" MacBook Pro in it.

There are two other compartments for storage and numerous small zipper pockets. On one side there is a water bottle holder, and on one of the shoulder straps a bottle opener (a standard feature of all Timbuk2 bags).

There's heavy padding on the back of the bag (where your back touches it) as well as on the shoulder straps.

As the the video shows, it's not a large bag, and that's the point. It's meant to hold your laptop and several documents -- whatever you may need to bring home from work for the night or the weekend. It's also small enough that if you're going out after work and you have it with you, it will easily fit under a table. And, it will fit under any airplane seat.

Finally, I also like that there's no indication that it's a laptop bag. In fact, if someone were going through it, they probably wouldn't even notice the laptop compartment in the back.
text_fidelity_b: TIMBUK2 Command Laptop Backpack, Black

Heated Gloves for Women Touchscreen Rechargeable Battery Electric Hand Warmers Winter Gloves Ski Gloves for Outdoor Sports Cycling Riding Skiing Skating I’ve never owned heated gloves before, but these are amazing! The design allows you to easily tighten several areas of the glove for a better fit, and you can still use your smart phone with the fingertips, which is great. The batteries have light indicators to show you roughly how charged they are, and they are easy to put in to the glove and remove, as well as to charge. Turning the gloves on and off it’s also as simple as the press of a button on top, which is easy to operate even while wearing the gloves.

As for the heat distribution, it’s not as even as I would like: it is most concentrated at the thumb and doesn’t distribute as much to the other areas. Even so, it’s incredibly soothing and pleasant, and on the most frigid days, boy does it make a difference! There are three levels of intensity for the heat, so you can decide what feels best. For me, I either like 45% or 70%. The hottest setting (100%), because it’s so concentrated in the thumb, feels a little uncomfortable for me personally. These were so straightforward on how to use them, I didn’t need the instruction manual, but I read it anyway just to see if I was missing anything. I learned there is a spare cable in case the one inside the glove wears out for whatever reason, which is nice.

Overall, these are excellent for cold weather and people whose hands get particularly cold. Even off-season, if you have arthritis or any hand pain, these are terrific for that as well. Terrific invention!
text_fidelity_b: Heated Gloves for Women Touchscreen Rechargeable Battery Electric Hand Warmers Winter Gloves Ski Gloves for Outdoor Sports Cycling Riding Skiing Skating

text_fidelity_a:
Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case I should have listened to the other 2 reviewers. I am beyond disappointed in the condition of this item. First of all, the fact that all the pieces were separate would not have been an issue IF the items were packed properly. The piece of sod was thrown haphazardly into a very thin plastic bag that was completely wide open and not secured closed at all. There is almost as much dirt and grass in the bottom of the bag as there is on the piece of sod. I'm surprised that there isn't dirt and grass all over the box it was thrown into as well. Worst of all, the sod is absolutely NOTHING like the picture. it is a 3 inch round piece of mostly dirt, that is not a rich dark brown as pictured, but a dried-out, tan-colored crumbling mess. And, the grass is long, sparse and a mix of pale green, yellow and brown. Not sure what the freeze-drying process is supposed to do, but the grass and dirt are so dry that you can't even breathe near it without pieces of grass and dirt falling off. What a mess! AND it smells pretty nasty too.

The letter of authenticity is trash (or at least it is to Steiner). It was thrown into the box along with the packing materials, without an envelope or any other protection. From being jostled around inside the shipping box, it is now crumpled and torn in at least three places along the side. Granted, it is a thicker-weight paper, but an envelope would have been nice (especially for the price). The letter says that the sod was removed on March 14, 2009 and that it is "unconditionally guaranteed" - whatever that means. It's difficult to tell if the signature of "Brandon Steiner" is signed in ink or a copy. I don't want to damage the signature trying to figure it out.

The case is actually a baseball case and comes in a "single baseball glass case" box. When I first opened the shipping box, I thought I'd been sent the wrong item. The case IS made of glass, not acrylic, and supposedly has a cherry wood base. It also is not nearly as nice as the picture depicts. The wood is dry and dull and the joints are roughly glued together and uneven. Unlike one of the other reviewers (and the description), I did not receive a separate sticker to apply to the base. It actually has a metal plaque already attached. The problem is, the only words that are legible are "Yankee Stadium Artifact." There are three full lines of smaller writing below that but it is completely unreadable. I can't tell if the words got scratched off or if it was improperly printed on the plate to begin with. I cannot read what it says at all.

I'm not familiar with these types of cases, but there is nothing that holds the grass in place. The bottom is a slick mirror, and the slightest movement causes the sod to slide around inside the case, leaving dirt and debris all over the bottom. Unless its kept perfectly still, it will probably fall apart completely into a big mess in no time. My biggest regret is that I did not purchase this from Amazon. I paid only $59 from another source who is not nearly as easy to deal with. Although, I don't think it would have made a difference in the quality of the product or awful packaging, because this item ships directly from Steiner sports anyway.

I've posted over 80 product reviews on Amazon. This is the first time I've ever felt the need to post pictures or video. This item is so pathetic - you really have to see it to believe it, so I am going to post something tomorrow. I just wanted to post my review ASAP so that anyone considering buying this as a last-minute Christmas gift is forewarned. I initially felt too embarrassed to give this as a gift, but now I think the recipient might appreciate the "tragic humor" of this item. It would make a good conversation piece for sure! I will let him decide if he wants to return it for something else, or keep it as something to show to his friends and laugh about.

text_fidelity_a:
HOZAN Spoke Threading Machine C700 This tool gets a bad rap, and unfairly, I think. Sure it takes time, but it works fine for the occasional wheel building project or replacement spoke. It's a nice item to have in the tool box for a rainy day when you can't be riding. You can build or repair a wheel instead. Even a bike shop might find one of these handy.

It's fairly simple. The tool mounts in a vise. The three rollers emboss threads in the spoke, rather than cut them. This makes for a stronger spoke. You turn the crank and the rollers "chase" threads up the spoke. When you get the threaded length you want, you turn the crank in reverse to back the rollers off the spoke.

I just used it to thread 36 14-gauge spokes, with no problems at all. (It threads 14 and 15 gauge spokes.)

The keys to using this tool successfully are to generously use cutting oil (or an equivalent), start with a properly chamfered spoke, and make several passes to get the depth of thread you want.

I think one reason this device gets such a bad rap is that people try to make it cut finished threads in one pass. If you tighten down the rollers that much to start, it will be difficult to get a blank spoke to feed into them.

Practice with a few extra spokes first. Chamfer the ends slightly with a file or a grinder.

Open up the Hozan tool's rollers by loosening the adjustment nut, until it will easily "take" a blank spoke and lightly emboss threads. Back the spoke out, tighten the nut a quarter to half turn, and make another pass through. Repeat this until you get threads embossed deeply enough so that a spoke nipple screws on easily for its full length. That will be your final setting.

Now you can back the adjustment nut off a full turn (360 degrees). This is so you can start a blank spoke. Make a first pass through, back the spoke out, tighten the adjustment nut a half turn, pass the spoke through and back out, and tighten it one half turn again for the final pass. Repeat this process for every spoke you want to thread. After a few you'll get into a rhythm and things will go faster. Apply more cutting oil with every spoke.

After every few spokes clean the rollers. I spray them with WD-40 while holding a folded paper towel underneath, then re-oil them for the next spoke.

The instructions say that with proper care this tool will last for years. I don't see any reason why it won't.
text_fidelity_b: HOZAN Spoke Threading Machine C700

text_fidelity_a:
Thule UpTake Hydration Pack [[VIDEOID:4efefdd0a4252dd270b43bf5abf224e1]] I have three hydration packs (see list below). Of the two I tested so far, I love this one the best. Note that this pack also does not come with instructions and I found that none of them do.

1 - This one - [[ASIN:B07MR4GJL8 Thule (pronounced Toolie) Uptake Hydration Pack, 8L with 2.5L Hydrapak--about 85 fluid ounces]] - superb pack; 5 stars
2 - [[ASIN:B07GHR1RSQ Osprey Women's Salida 8 (about 85 ounces)]] - excellent pack; 4 stars
3 - [[ASIN:B07HJVD4GX CamelBak M.U.L.E. LR 15 100oz]] - I have not tested this one yet

After using this Thule, I absolutely love it even more than my Osprey. It is extremely well designed, comfortable, and stylish and has a cavernous interior for storage.

PROS
- There are several loops all over the pack including one on the bottom that can be used to affix a bike light, hang a helmet with a carbiner, etc.

- There's an outer zippered pocket to store small items such as a cell phone, Chapstick, tissues, etc.

- The main pocket has one mesh zippered pocket next to the hydration bladder that can be used for a cell phone or similarly sized items. There is a large storage area in front of that for a wallet, shirt, or other personal effects for the day.

- Behind the inner zippered pocket is the compartment for the hydration bladder.

- The hydration bladder is 2.5L or about 85 ounces. The pack has a tiny cloth loop that holds the bladder upright when full so that it does not sink to the bottom of the pack. All I had to do was unhook the bladder, slide off the clip, pull it apart like a Zip-lock bag, then fold over with the tracks facing outward, and slip on the clip to close. Note that it is possible to fold the bladder the wrong way. Make sure the fold has the tracks facing out on both sides. Once the bladder is closed, re-attach it to the cloth loop.

- The pack has adjustable waist and chest belts.

- The tubing to the reservoir has a magnetic track that keeps it in place along the chest area of the pack. This is absolutely wonderful even though the track and bite valve faces down and not up toward the mouth. Therefore, when biking, one has to grab the tubing to drink. There is also another loop and clip through which the tubing passes.

- The bite valve is removable for drying. It also has a locking mechanism to lock it so that water does not seep out.

- The pack has padding in the shoulder and lumbar region for extra comfort.

CONS
- This comes with zero instructions but since this is not my first pack, I had no trouble operating this pack.

- My major complaint is that the water coming out of the bladder tastes awful. It tastes like a new shower curtain smells. I was told that I could partially fill the bladder with water and squeeze lemon juice into it and then freeze it to get rid of the taste. I have not tried that yet. This is typical of ALL hydration bladders I tried, unfortunately.

Overall, I love the way this pack is engineered and how comfortable it is to use. Its simplicity is its biggest virtue along with the magnetic tubing track to keep the tubing in place. I used this once so far on a two-hour walk and I did not even know I was wearing this. The bite value is easily accessible but does face down. This means a biker would have to grab it and bring it toward the mouth to use. Drying the bladder between use requires that I stuff the bladder mouth with a silicone ramekin and hang it upside down for several days. It takes about three to four days to dry since this hydration bladder has two halves on the interior.

Video - My recorder is awful; I apologize for the blurriness. Please note that the hydration bladder is 2.5L and the 8L refers to the cargo space and not the reservoir.

Photo 1 is of the specifications.

Photos 2-5 is of the pack.

Photo 6 shows the bladder.

Photo 7 shows the bladder opening. Note that I inserted a Kiwi cutter into the mouth of the bladder to show where the opening is so I could take a picture. However, that green item DOES NOT come with this pack.
text_fidelity_b: Thule UpTake Hydration Pack

Fitarc Pull Up Assist Bands,Pull Up Resistance Bands for Chin Up,Adjustable Pullup Bands I remember as a young man I used to be able to do 10 pull ups. 30+ years later, I tried to do a pull-up and couldn't even do one - not even half of one, actually. It's been 6 months, and I am still working on 2. Someone told me that this is because I'm not going through the whole pull-up motion often enough to build the muscles and that I should go to a gym and use a machine that gives you an assist so you can go through repetitions of the whole motion - over time, the assist is then reduced without reducing the number of repetitions. Well, I live too far from a gym - so I got these assist bands. And the first time I tried them after installation, I did 5 pull-ups - and could have done more! Starting tomorrow I will do 10 pull-ups and then reduce the number of straps over time.

The only downside to this solution is that if you don't have your pull-up bars installed high enough, you have to fiddle around with the strap length or put your knees in the stirrup instead of the feet. But that's not the bands' fault.
text_fidelity_b: Fitarc Pull Up Assist Bands,Pull Up Resistance Bands for Chin Up,Adjustable Pullup Bands

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Stash It Belt One of the most frustrating things for me is if I want to go for a long walk in a rural area and I have to have a phone near by. I prefer to walk without a phone and such, but at times I can not escape the need to have a phone for an important phone call. I really don't like a fanny pack, as it is really big, but was looking for something handier.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This stash belt is very thin. It is deceiving, however. The belt itself is a good quality stretchy elastic. It is heavy duty but not so heavy that it is bulky. There is a black clip in the back, and a slide to make the belt longer or shorter. The pack itself is 2 inches by 9 inches. However, it has a pleat in the top and bottom which make it bigger.

There is a water resistant lining in the pack, a front zipper, and a very thin reflective strip on the front. At full length, the belt measures 34 inches unstretched, and 41 inches stretched. The shortest is 24 inches stretching to about 32 inches.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
When using this, I can put my smart phone into the pack, a set of keys and a few cards. I can also stick in a tissue or two folded small. A huge set of keys will make it a bit tight, but a reasonable ring of keys with several keys on it should be fine. The pack does stretch a little bit so that things will fit.

As far as use, I found that this is very handy. I have to stretch it a little tight so that it does not bobble around as I walk. That is okay though, because it holds it in place. Otherwise, the phone and things can make it sag a little bit. Finding the right tightness takes a bit of trial and error. I really appreciate having this as it makes it the closet to walking without anything that I have been able to get.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I really like this stash belt. It is handy, useful, and makes it so that I can go for long walks without bulky bags or packs. Safe and with decent capacity, I can carry what I want to have with me yet feel free and lightweight at the same time. With a range of sizes it will fit, many people would benefit from this, but if you are a big and tall man, it might be a bit tight.

RATING
Five stars for this. I really like it. It is handy and easy to use. I will update if I have anything else important to add in the future.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Stash It Belt

text_fidelity_a:
Elvira 32oz Large Water Bottle with Motivational Time Marker & Removable Strainer,Fast Flow BPA Free Non-Toxic for Fitness, Gym and Outdoor Sports For whatever reason, mine did not come with the strainer. If it did, I'd likely not have used it anyway, as I don't find a need to add fruit to my water. But since it was supposed to, I need to mention it. For some, it may be the very reason you select it. Product description states to contact them if there are any issues.

The bottle itself is solid. Holds a little over 32 ounces, has markings to help guide you in adequate water consumption, and the plastic is BPA free. I have other water bottle brand/style that I prefer-especially for carrying around with me, but this one has been good for use in the house through the day.

The bottle and lid is simple. The top screws on. There is a flip top with an opening approximately size of a quarter to drink from. If you want a larger opening, just unscrew the lid entirely. I prefer to do the latter to as it is easier for me to guzzle down some water that way. The wide open bottle is nice for cleaning purpose. And stuffing bottle with ice.

A good sized carry strap for convenience.

While the bottle cap feels secure, I am not inclined to toss this in a bag like my preferred water bottle. I am not too sure how well the flip top would stay on. I could be wrong, but I don't want to risk it. For me, this is strictly for around the house use. That being said..

I don't have too much trouble getting my water intake. I'm not on a diet, I have never noticed that drinking water helps with any of that, but I do prefer to stay hydrated and also simply enjoy plain cold water. Of all the bad choices I make for myself, I tend to always choose water to drink. I am a champ with getting my water in all summer, but I do slow up a bit come winter. I keep a 32 ounce bottle on me all day, and I even have another one at my bedside. This bottle is also 32 ounces (actually a little more, since the 32 ounce line is a few inches from top). The difference between my other bottles and this one, is that there is a little motivating factor through the use of time stamped on the bottle. The idea is to fill the bottle twice to get the recommended water intake. I thought if anything, this is what might remind me to keep drinking my water as we head into winter months. I wasn't sure if I was going to pay much attention to it enough to help me, but I find that the first thing I do in the morning is to fill my bottle to the top. I usually guzzle down 16 ounces almost immediately, After that, it is just a matter of looking at my bottle through the day, paying attention to the time, and making a point to take a good long drink. Refill and repeat. A simple, handy thing. My preferred bottles don't have that :)

And so, I am sold on the effectiveness of the time stamp. A little thing, but it does help. I don't need motivational quotes, just the easy at a glance view of my water level and the time. Good for me!

So I see no reason not to be happy with this bottle- unless you don't get the filter like me. . It is reasonably priced, good sized capacity that is easy to work with (basically drain and fill twice!). Cap off makes it easy to drink down a bunch of water, or just flip the cap to take swigs as needed. If you find yourself not drinking enough at once, I recommend drinking from wider opening.

Bottle is wide, may or may not fit in your vehicle cup holder, and as for carrying around casually in a bag.. still not sure how secure it is. It isn't subpar, just be mindful. Even with that consideration I recommend it, and consider it a 4.5-5 star product (if stays under $15)
text_fidelity_b: Elvira 32oz Large Water Bottle with Motivational Time Marker & Removable Strainer,Fast Flow BPA Free Non-Toxic for Fitness, Gym and Outdoor Sports

Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks… I had high hopes for these electric socks. I mean, electric blankets have been around forever, right? So maybe, just maybe these would work. Sadly, they are utter crap.

When they arrived, they didn't look too bad. I was concerned about how much of the sock would have a heated area, but I figured, even a relatively small area might be helpful. I got some fresh AA batteries and loaded up the battery compartments. (There is a little pocket near the top outer side of each sock. There is a wire inside each of these that connects to the battery box.)

I felt just the faintest bit of warmth from one sock and nothing from the other. I put them on and honestly could not tell a difference between the non-working side and the one that was faintly warm. I thought perhaps they needed more time to warm up, so I continued wearing them hoping that would happen. I was busy working and after a couple of hours realized that they had never warmed up. So I decided to check the batteries, 'just in case,' they weren't fully charged. When I checked them on my battery tester, all four were completely dead even though I had gotten them from my fresh supply. I wondered if they could possibly have been bad to begin with, though that seemed highly unlikely. Then I wondered if the box had somehow drained the batteries.

Still holding out a tiny bit of hope the socks would warm, I got out more batteries. This time I checked them with my battery tester first, to make sure they were fully charged. They were. Again I felt the tiniest bit of warmth and thought, "Great! I guess the last batch of batteries were no good."

Put them on and again, could not feel the warmth. I later checked the fully charged batteries and .. you guessed it, they were drained. So not only did the stupid socks not work, they somehow drained EIGHT AA batteries!! What a waste of time and money. Needless to say, I want to send these back.

It's really a shame because a lot of people would love to have socks like this if they would actually work. I hope the manufacturer figures out a way to make them work AND do so without having to go through dozens of batteries each week.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks…

text_fidelity_a:
SE Survivor Series Portable Chain Saw with Ergonomic Handles - CS001 I like to do a lot of outside work. That includes cutting down dead wood and keeping a rather large yard in order. I don't tend to use a lot of power tools as the guys all have their own which they take with them. That has left me with little to work with. I got this little hand portable chain saw not only for survival, but to use around my property when I need to cut some significant wood. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a rather hard to get into package. Once I was able to cut into it, I found that it has two handles with cord on them, a chain for sawing and a nylon carrying case with a belt loop on it to keep it handy.

HOW DOES THIS GO TOGETHER?
The handles slip through the rings on either end of this saw. It is important that you lay the chain out before installing the handles so that you have the handles in the right direction so that you can pull on them and the saw blades will be going into the wood.

Once you have them in the right direction (and both facing the same way) then you slip the loop into the ring and over the handle and it stays put.

HOW DO YOU USE IT?
You put the blades into the branch you want to cut, cross the handles in front of the branch and pull from side to side to keep the chain moving back and forth.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is a GREAT SAW! I don't have tons of body strength, but this saw has regularly cut through 3 and 4 inch wood for me. I LOVE how fast it is. It only takes me a few minutes most of the time unless it is a very hard piece of wood.

CAN YOU CUT ALREADY CUT WOOD?
This does not work that well if the branch is already cut unless you can brace it into place and have a good resistance to keep it stable while you saw it. I find it is best when used on a branch still attached to a tree most of the time, or a really large part of a tree that might be dead, but it stays put.

OILING
I use a lubricant from our freeze dryer which is made for vacuum motors. It works really great and the one I use is food safe so it won't hurt the environment like fuel will. Small amount, not really worth discussing for most people, but it sure beats smelling like petroleum oil in the case.

CASE
The case is big enough for the saw to fit into, but I tend to keep a plastic bag in there to put the chain into to keep it from leaking through the case over time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a fabulous little saw. I love having it around. I have used it a lot and really am thankful to have it. Camping, hiking, or just working around the yard when the power tools are missing make this one of my favorite new tools I own.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. SO HAPPY to have this. If it is kept lubricated and not left out in the weather, this should last a while, perhaps only the handle cords might need replacing over time.
text_fidelity_b: SE Survivor Series Portable Chain Saw with Ergonomic Handles - CS001

text_fidelity_a:
Tennis Headbands for Men, Sweat Bands Headbands Men(3 Pack) for Yoga Gym Running Cycling Basketball Workout Accessories Stretchy Moisture Wicking Sweat Band for Women… UPDATE: I’ve been able to get back to working out and wearing these headbands while lifting weights, hitting a heavy bag, and on walks. In all cases they work out great and do as intended. I’ve been keeping the sweat out of my eyes and staying comfortable. Please read the rest of the review where I address why I still can’t give them 5 stars.

First, I grabbed these Tennis Headbands for Men, Under Armour Headbands Men(3 Pack) because I tend to seat a lot when working out and am tired of the sweat dripping down my face and into my eyes. I thought they looked cool.

I have debated on 4 or 5 stars, which I address below.

1. So, they do look as cool in person. My wife is not a big fan of headbands - thinks they look weird - but she saw them and immediately said they looked great. I agree. I like the solid black, but I equally like the patterns. Happy to wear them from that standpoint. The material feel nice. I find them comfortable on. To this point I think they are 5 stars.

NOTE: I strained my knee badly and have been off it for a week and told I need to give it several more days. therefore, I have not been able to wear them during a workout yet. I will come back and update IF they are anything but great. To this point I can only give 4 stars, with 5 a possibility.

2. Under Armour??? I am a big UA fan with a lot of UA gear. The title on the product page caught my attention, but mainly because 1. I love UA and 2. I did not see any UA logos on the product page. The headbands themselves do not have the UA logo. So I am confused as to why they are allowed to use the Under Armour brand name when as far as I can tell, they are nothing of the kind. To this point, I have to give them 4 stars. Without them being actual Under Armour they are still a fine product, but I am not okay with using the brand name when from everything I can tell, these are not made by nor sold by UA. My wife and I have both looked at all 3 headbands separately and together - there is NO Under Armour logo or labeling.

3. The sizing is mostly the same, but... I found that the solid and the blue pattern are the same size. I have a larger head (usually a baseball hat L-XL), but in this case while they fit spot on, the black pattern was slightly larger. Not working out, merely having them all, it was fine, but I will be curious if they all stay on the same. A smaller ahed might have an issue with the one, but I “think” smaller heads would be okay with the two. To this point I decide to go with a 4 star, as they are not consistent and I do expect them to be.

4. I cannot speak to their ability to keep the sweat off. My injury happened shortly after I ordered these and before they arrived, so that’s kept me from using them for their intended purpose. So right now I can only give them a 4 star rating. But to be fair, even if they come back 100% as expected, I am still bothered enough by the use of the Under Armour name - a brand name I do use often - on the product page when nothing on the actual product indicates they are UA - such as the UA logo. Therefore, for me, I could still not give these a full 5 star rating as I consider this action deceptive. This is a personal opinion and is mentioned here so as to fully explain why I would still consider this a 4 star product.

In the end I do - so far - like these headbands and think I’ll get some good use out of them. But Would rather they not use a brand name to promote them. When you literally write - Tennis Headbands for Men, Under Armour Headbands Men(3 Pack) as the title of the product then I expect they would be an Under Armour product and again, I cannot find any evidence of this being the case on the actual headbands. As stated above, my wife and I have both looked at all 3 headbands separately and together - there is NO Under Armour logo or labeling.
text_fidelity_b: Tennis Headbands for Men, Sweat Bands Headbands Men(3 Pack) for Yoga Gym Running Cycling Basketball Workout Accessories Stretchy Moisture Wicking Sweat Band for Women…

text_fidelity_a:
Stamina Magnetic Fusion Recumbent Exercise Bike When the bike arrived it was barely holding onto life. The box was all but beat to death and the only reason it had not spilt all its contents while in transit was the plastic straps.

Opening and sorting the parts was really easy, it comes in two major pieces. The instructions were relatively easy to follow using just the illustrations. The problems start to come when it's time to fasten the two pieces together (front and back). If you're not perfectly careful you will rip, break and strip the wires that go from the rear handlebar to the front control unit. As careful as I was (had read other reviews saying the same thing) the wires still stripped and broke, leaving me to jerry rig the wires by re stripping and taping them back together then hoping it would not happen again. The next major issue is the bolting of the center beam into the rear part of the bike. The faring has enough space between the actual holes that the bolt goes in that if you don't perfectly align and insert the bolt on the first try, the bolt and 2 washers fall into the bike and the only way you can get them out is to take off the entire faring which is a major pain and I ended up stripping two screws in the process. If you can get past this it's pretty much a cruise to the finish line except some small confusing issues with attaching the front handlebar assembly. Total time investing assembling = 2 hours.

The bike itself is very nice if it is not destroyed during shipping and survives the assembly process. It is sturdy, comfortable and quiet. The oversize lcd display is colorful and easy to read. I only wish they would have put the power plug on the rear of the bike instead of the front, but that would probably open a new can of worms trying to put it together including the risk of electric shock if the frayed wire came in contact with the frame!

All together very pleased with its performance and look. I am 6'5" tall and nearly 280 pounds. On the max seat adjustment in height I over extend my knees so I keep it one notch lower and it's perfect. I'd give this 5 stars but the assembly was so bad I had to give it 4.
text_fidelity_b: Stamina Magnetic Fusion Recumbent Exercise Bike

These Ryno-Tuff Resistance Bands Set are inexpensive and offer a good selection of bands, and - as most sets do - they come with a pair of handles, a pair of ankle straps and a door anchor. The set also includes a bag and a sturdy wall poster of exercises which those new to resistance band training could find very useful.

Let me get one thing out of the way first. The bag is small, and while you could carefully fold up all the bands and stuff the bag to make them fit, I'm not going to use the bag as putting everything into it is a pain. I'll use another bag I have that's more than twice the size so I can get to everything quickly during workouts.

Now the bands themselves. First off, they work, offering a decent amount of resistance per band. I find the material thinner than with brands like Bodylastics, which I used for years and will probably use again. If you pinch one of the thinner Ryno tubes and then one of the Bodylastics tubes, you'll notice the walls of the Ryno tubes are thinner, and don't have the snap-proof cord inside each band. That being said, Bodylastics sets cost more. These Ryno bands will get the job done, although I'm guessing that they won't last as long.

The handles are nicely padded, a plus, although the fabric used for the parts you don't grip is on the thin side, and if I were planning to go heavy with this site, I'd buy stronger handles. The ankle straps are about the same quality you get with some other resistance band sets. If you don't work heavy, they should be fine. I tore the last, very similar set I had working out at about 75 pounds, and bought something studier. I suggest you try these and see how they do for you.

But here's the thing. I have a functional trainer and weights in the house. I prefer resistance bands for certain exercises, and if you want to work out at the beach, in the park or in a hotel room, this is where resistance bands shine. If you travel a lot and prefer to work out in your hotel room, a set of resistance bands takes up little space, doesn't weigh much and are easy to use. Want to catch some rays while you work out or just want to enjoy the outdoors? Resistance bands. And if you don't have room, they're also one of the better, lower cost options.

I'll be honest - these aren't the best quality resistance bands I've used, but they're also far from the worst, and they're inexpensive, which is a plus. They allow you to stack your resistance, the handles are comfy, and the door anchor is pretty good, too. I wouldn't expect these to last as long as more premium bands, but if you don't overstretch them, they should last a while. I'm happy I got them, and I'll be using them for a while. If you're just getting into shape, the poster will be helpful, and if you travel, this set could help you work out anywhere.
text_fidelity_b: Ryno Tuff 12 Pc Resistance Bands Set - 5 Workout Bands, Cushioned Ankle Straps, Padded Handles, Door Anchor & Waterproof Gym Bag - Home Exercise, Strength Training, Physical Therapy, Yoga Fitness Gear

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Discontinued Osprey Salida 8 Women's Bike Hydration Backpack with Hydraulics Reservoir, Teal Glass [[VIDEOID:f899b5904dd638d027a40416fde9e9f1]] This is my first hydration pack and it does not come with any instructions. It took me about one hour to figure everything out--particularly the hydration bladder. However, after using this, I love it. It is extremely well designed, comfortable, and stylish. I also love the color.

PROS
- There's a loop for a light on the bottom of the pack.

- It has a bike helmet clip.

- There's an outer pocket to store clothing.

- The inner pocket has one covered zippered pocket for cell phone, Chapstick, etc. There's also a mesh zippered pocket below that and another folder-like pocket opposite that in addition to the main compartment area for minimal storage.

- Behind the inner pocket is the zippered compartment for the hydration bladder.

- The hydration bladder is 2.5L or 85 ounces. It comes with a handle and the pack has a tiny cinch strap that holds the bladder upright when full so that it does not sink to the bottom of the pack. I did a search on YouTube for "How to fill Osprey Hydration pack," and found Chris SERF's very helpful video. Prior to viewing that video I just could not figure out how to open the main bladder compartment after I got the slide cinch off the bladder.

- The pack has a waist belt and a chest belt with magnetic closure.

- The tubing to the reservoir has a magnetic disk that clips it onto the chest belt area of the pack. There are also various loops through which the tubing can pass.

- The bite valve is removable. Another YouTuber said there is a locking mechanism to lock the bite valve but I could not get it to lock. Sometimes water will leak out of the bite valve but I only had that happen once.

- It has a mesh back to increase air flow which reduces but does not eliminate sweating against the pack.

CONS
- This comes with zero instructions and I could not find a video on the Osprey website on how to fill the hydration bladder. As of this writing, there are also no manuals for the Salida under the customer support section.

- The tubing is about two inches too short for my build. Since the card that came with the pack says the tubing can be cut, I think the tubing should be lengthened as it can always be made shorter but it is impossible to make longer.

- My major complaint is that the water coming out of the bladder tastes awful. It tastes like a new shower curtain smells. I was only able to drink about half a cup as I kept spitting it out. I wrote and tweeted Osprey and they have not yet responded with a solution. However, the YouTuber, Chris MORSF, whose video helped me learn how to open the bladder said that the "Only thing that I can think of is Steriliser tablets like what is used for babies bottles then giving the bladder a very thorough rinse out with water." I have yet to try that.

Overall, I love the way this pack is engineered and how comfortable it is. I used this once so far on a two-hour walk and I did not even know I was wearing this. I had a concern of drying the bladder between use but came up with my own solution of stuffing the bladder mouth with a silicone ramekin (see last photo) and hanging it upside down for several days. It dried in two days and the tubing is almost dry as of day three. If Osprey addressed all three CONS and provided instructions or a link to instructions for a neophyte user like me and how to get rid of that bad taste, I would have rated this five stars. I attached a video that I hope is helpful and some pictures of this Osprey Salida 8 Women's pack.

UPDATE May 14, 2019 - I finally heard from Osprey regarding the two questions I had. I have yet to try either solution.

1 – To get rid of the disgusting plastic flavor of the water, they recommend freezing the reservoir with lemon juice to clean it out. They also have cleaning tablets available that help with the taste.

2- With regard to the bite valve lock being unmovable, they recommend running it under hot water and then twisting it.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Discontinued Osprey Salida 8 Women's Bike Hydration Backpack with Hydraulics Reservoir, Teal Glass

text_fidelity_a:
Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black i'm not a police officer so i might not make the demands on this light that they do, or find the same programming options useful. that said, i like this light a lot. while it falls just shy of perfect for me, it does come very close and i imagine i'll be content to rely on this light for many years to come.

the construction is as solid as i imagine the construction of any flashlight could be. the light feels like a solid hunk of metal in the hand, which, when all screwed together and ready to go, it pretty much is. it has a glass lens on the front end (of course), a rubber-covered push-button switch on the back end, and a removable metal pocket clip on the side, and these features aside, its construction is entirely of very solid, heavy-duty metal. if you're familiar with Maglites, this light is like a Mini Maglite...but on some very serious steroids. indeed, i carried Mini Maglites on my belt for years, and whenever i'd misplace one, as i did periodically, i'd go back to the big orange store (for some reason i never figured out that i should buy my flashlights on Amazon) and shop for a new one, excited all over again about buying (the small version of) the same tough flashlight as used by police and other official-type people who rely on their lights in some very serious situations. well the Streamlight 88040 ProTAC HL makes the once-venerable Maglite look like lightweight consumer-grade fluff by comparison. gone are my days of needing two hands (or the still-less-desirable alternative of one hand and my teeth) to turn my light on; gone too are the days of sometimes wishing my light was brighter. oh yes, and lest i forget: also gone are the days of going to turn on my light and finding it won't turn on because the butt cap has come loose and lost contact with the batteries. this happened repeatedly with my last Mini Maglite, no matter how hard i'd screwed on the butt cap, and was a source of great exasperation, especially when i wanted light in a hurry. that isn't going to happen with the Streamlight - once you screw this thing together, it's *solid.* and the light output on the high setting puts Mini Maglites to shame - including the new higher-intensity ones.

my main complaints about this light are minor. as another reviewer said, i'd like it to have more programs; the program that would give me all three beam types while making the most sense for the way i use the light - low / high / strobe - isn't available on this model; in order to have both low and high intensity steady beams available, you need to either have the light turn on initially at high intensity and then jump past the strobe to get from high to low (high / strobe / low program), or you have to forego the strobe altogether (low / high program). i'm sure the high / strobe / low program works well for law enforcement, and that *is* who this light was designed for, but Streamlight would only broaden their market appeal by adding a low / high / strobe program. i guess cops don't want their targets to be able to strobe them back that easily.

another complaint is about the design and quality of the included holster. the Mini Maglite's holster, while given to flopping around a bit more, is superior in design and quality to the one supplied with this light. the belt loop on this light's holster is too low, so that if you carry the light head-upward, the light / holster rig is top-heavy and pulls away from your belt - and starts pulling the holster away from its own belt loop - as soon as you put it on; after just a week or two of owning this light i found the threads holding the holster to its belt loop were giving out and the holster was tearing away from the loop. i guess you could carry the light head-down, but that puts the velcro flap at the bottom, underneath the light, and i don't like relying that heavily on the velcro flap staying closed to prevent my light from dropping out onto the ground. i might try the belt clip for a while to see if i can make that work as well for me...but i much prefer a good holster.

finally, another reviewer pointed out that the low-intensity beam is actually strobing at a speed imperceptible to our vision under most conditions, but that this strobing can make moving things, like machinery, appear to be moving more slowly than they really are, moving not at all, or moving backwards, and that that creates a potentially dangerous situation. i don't like that, i'm grateful to that reviewer for pointing it out, and i just hope i never forget about that phenomenon when doing so could pose a threat to my safety.
text_fidelity_b: Streamlight 88066 Pro Tac Rail Mount HL-X 1000-Lumen Professional Tactical Flashlight with High/Low/Strobe Dual Fuel, Black

Relentless Tactical The Defender Leather IWB Holster - Fits Most 1911 Style Handguns - Kimber - Colt - S & W - Sig Sauer - Remington - Ruger & More - Made in USA Relentless Tactical is well-known for it's reasonably priced yet high quality holsters. This particular model is designed to fit "most 1911 style handguns". What I found out is a bit different. This holster is very particular with which pistols it provides the right fit for. Although some of the larger guns can be slipped inside it, there is not a tight enough fit to hold these guns when the holster is held upside down.

What I did find that seems to fit well include the following: Kahr CM9, Glock 42, Colt Defender, and surprisingly my old Cobray double barrel .410/45LC derringer. Of course trying to withdraw and safely shoot this derringer in a tactical situation could lead to some potentially horrible mistakes. If indeed you manage to get that gun safely on target, the person on the receiving end would probably faint just from the fireball.

Although I tried several others in my collection (Glock 19, Colt Commander, Walther P22, Springfield XDS, H&K VP9SK, etc.) none of them properly/safely fit this holster. The next step up would be important and I'm sure that Relentless would be happy to point you in the correct direction. They also offer a 100% satisfaction guarantee with no questions asked. Good people to deal with!
text_fidelity_b: Relentless Tactical The Defender Leather IWB Holster - Fits Most 1911 Style Handguns - Kimber - Colt - S & W - Sig Sauer - Remington - Ruger & More - Made in USA

UV 50+ Protection Outdoor Multifunctional Flap Hat Neck Protection Cap with Removable Sun Shield and Mask Perfect for Fishing Hiking Garden Work Activities Being blond and light skinned is a bit of a hazard living in Southwest Florida. Add in allergies to grass and pollen and you've got a potential disaster waiting every time you mow the lawn. If I knew then what I know now, I would have done a much better job protecting myself from the sun over the past 60 years. Now the cumulative damage is putting my Dermatologist's kids through college--and maybe medical school.

Besides wearing hats, sunglasses, and using zinc oxide and 50+ UV sunscreen, I decided to invest the princely sum of $10.39 to try out this flap hat. Turns out to be just what the doctor(s) might have ordered. The hat and flaps protect my head and neck, the front mesh keeps pollen and dust from entering my mouth, and the hat can be adjusted/manipulated to fit your needs. Add in that it's made of a lightweight (and breathable) material and has 50+ UV protection, and you're talking more about a hat "system" instead of just a hat.

Use a good pair of sunglasses and some zinc oxide (if you wear the front flap lower), a lightweight long-sleeved shirt and pants, and you've got great protection against the elements. An added bonus is the protection the hat and flaps give you from mosquitos and biting flies. The less distractions the better when you're running power equipment. If you're looking for extra protection from the sun at a very reasonable price, this is your hat.
text_fidelity_b: UV 50+ Protection Outdoor Multifunctional Flap Hat Neck Protection Cap with Removable Sun Shield and Mask Perfect for Fishing Hiking Garden Work Activities

I self-censored the review too but did have to mention that Nike Match Vapor kits were far superior. Yet the Puma customer service team had it yanked.. Lame. So I’m expanding upon what I wrote here with no holds barred.

I only wear the Player/Authentic kits while working out as I always prefer the better material. I have bought at least one Nike Match/Vapor Kit from City over the past four years and have absolutely loved the texture and sweat-wicking ability they all had. Yes, they are massively expensive for us here in the US ($160+) but ponied up for them nonetheless.

So I was super disappointed with Puma's first foray into City gear.. When I received my order almost immediately upon first touch I could tell this was a sub-par kit. In fact I wondered if it was a Stadium/Fan kit.. Nope, this was the player model and knew within a minute I’d be returning it.. One thing that was good was the fit.. These aren’t scuba-skin tight so that was nice but they still looked garbage.. It doesn’t help I personally think Puma royally F’d up and decided to desecrate the home kit with that god-awful purple strips. Just horrendous in every way imaginable.. I can only say the person who designed this kit (And especially the disgusting 3rd kit) really, really, really hate City.
